column1: # SALLY LEIBHOLZ WAS NEVER A BERLIN HOUSEHOLDER, AND THE PRE-1903 DIRECTORIES ARE UNDER ANOTHER NUMBER.
# Berliner Adressbuch, Zentral- und Landesbibliothek Berlin. Rows 264 and 242. Read 11 October 2026.
# WHY IT WAS RUN. Row 264 — Sally Leibholz's death — costed the Szubin route and called it bad value:
# 190 death units across three registry offices, NO alphabetical death index, and one Leibholz in the
# portal's index of 228,278 people. Its instruction was "TRY BERLIN FIRST": Kurt was born there in
# 1912, the household is at Chodowieckistraße in 1913, Jacob married there in 1924, so if Sally
# followed his sons to Berlin his death is a Berlin death. The test is whether he is in the directory.
field
# ---------------- THE INSTRUMENT HAD A HOLE IN IT AND NOBODY HAD NOTICED ----------------
*** THE ANCHOR THIS ARCHIVE HAS USED FOR THREE WEEKS COVERS 1903 TO 1943, NOT 1799 TO 1943 ***
column2: PI 34115495 is the Berliner Adreßbuch at ZLB and its own record says YEAR [1903, 1943]. Every query for 1902 or earlier returns ZERO PAGES — and the control proves it is the anchor and not the surname, because SCHMIDT returns zero in those years too. A note in data/berlin-adressbuch-names.tsv has said "volumes 1799 to 1970" since September. IT IS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE.

column1: *** THE EARLIER VOLUMES ARE UNDER PI 34115512, AND THEY RUN 1873 TO 1896 ***
AND THERE IS A SIX-YEAR HOLE: 1897 TO 1902 ARE NOT DIGITISED AT ALL
column2: not under 34115512, which stops at 1896, and not under 34115495, which starts at 1903. Both return zero pages and zero controls. ANY BERLIN DIRECTORY QUESTION ABOUT 1897-1902 IS UNANSWERABLE AT ZLB and this archive should stop expecting an answer from it.

column1: *** THERE IS NO SALLY LEIBHOLZ IN ANY BERLIN DIRECTORY FROM 1903 TO 1920 ***
column2: the Leibholz Namenteil run was pulled for 1903, 1905, 1908, 1910, 1913, 1916 and 1920. THESE VOLUMES PRINT FULL FORENAMES, not initials, and the runs come out legibly: Adolf · Albert · Arthur · Cäsar · Curt · Else · Felix · Franz · Georg · Ida · Julie · Julius · Leo · Louis · Max · Nathan · Oscar · Paul · Siegfried · Th. · William. NOT ONE SALLY AND NOT ONE SALOMON.

column1: and the 1916 run was read at the page image to earn that
column2: PI 34115495_1916, page order 1710, the run read at 2.6x with the forenames in the frame — Felix · S. · Georg · Julius · Leo · Leo · Max · Max · Oscar · WILLIAM · Max · Franz · Th. · M. Leibholz · Albert · Else. The only "S." in it is the hat business and that is Samuel, below. THE TEXT LAYER AND THE IMAGE AGREE ENTRY FOR ENTRY, which is what licenses the other six years being taken from the text layer.

column1: *** WHAT THAT MEANS, STATED NARROWLY ***
column2: A MAN WHO IS NOT A HOUSEHOLDER IS NOT IN THE DIRECTORY. Sally would have been 56 in 1903 and 73 in 1920; a man of that age living with a son, in an institution, or as a lodger would not be printed. SO THIS IS NOT PROOF THAT HE NEVER CAME TO BERLIN. What it is: the only cheap instrument for placing him there has been run across eighteen years and returns nothing, and ROW 264'S "TRY BERLIN FIRST" NO LONGER HAS ANYTHING BEHIND IT.

column1: and the pre-1900 volumes cannot be asked the question at all
column2: 1873 to 1896 give FORENAME INITIALS ONLY — "A., Beamter", "O., Lederhdl.", "J., Ww." — and single-letter initials are the worst-OCR'd thing on a Fraktur directory page. A negative on a forename cannot be drawn from them. WHAT THEY DO GIVE is the surname's whole presence in the city: six to eight Leibholz households through the 1890s, of which the constants are LOUIS (Posamentier- und Kurzwaren-Engros, Klosterstraße then Bischofstraße 10), O. (Lederhändler, Dresdener Straße 118/119) and L. (Rentiere, Willibald-Alexis-Straße 22) — plus, from 1895, LEIBHOLZ & BERNSTEIN, Bank- und Kommissionsgeschäft für Immobilien, W Behrenstraße 11, "Inh. Ad. Leibholz (Friedenau) u. H. Bernstein".

column1: # ---------------- FOUR THINGS THE SWEEP TURNED UP ON THE WAY, ALL READ AT THE IMAGE IN 1916 ----------------
*** SAMUEL'S HAT BUSINESS IS SEVENTEEN YEARS OLDER THAN THIS ARCHIVE THOUGHT ***
column2: — S., Hüte, SW 19, Jerusalemer Str. 5. 6 — T. Ztr. 6128. IN THE 1916 VOLUME. data/berlin-adressbuch-names.tsv dates the firm's Jerusalemer Straße address to 1933 and says it moved to Kommandantenstraße 29 by 1936. IT WAS AT JERUSALEMER STRASSE IN 1916, in the First World War, under the same initial the 1940 and 1941 volumes would use for a different reason.

column1: *** WILLIAM OWNED KURFÜRSTENDAMM 169 AND 170 ***
column2: — William, Kaufm., W 15, Kurfürstendamm 169 u. 170 E. T. Pfzb. 3448, 2—4. [BK.] — the "E." is EIGENTÜMER. This archive held "William, Kaufm., W15 Kurfürstendamm 169" for 1913 and did not have the second house or the ownership. Row 242's William is a Charlottenburg factory owner in 1903 and the owner of two Kurfürstendamm houses in 1916.

column1: *** A SECOND LEIBHOLZ HOUSEHOLD IN CHODOWIECKISTRASSE ***
column2: — Else, geb. Kabelitz, Lageristin, NO 55, Chodowieckistr. 8 I. beside "— Georg, Kaufm., NO 55, Chodowieckistr. 31 III." data/chodowieckistrasse-1913.tsv has Georg at no. 31 in 1913 and nobody else in the street. THERE ARE TWO, at numbers 8 and 31, in 1916. Else is a LAGERISTIN, a warehouse clerk, and "geb. Kabelitz" is a maiden name this archive has never held.

column1: and a trade that dates itself
column2: — Max, Kaufm., Wilmersdf., Kurfürstendamm Nr. 149 … siehe MAX LEIBHOLZ, HEERES-AUSRÜSTUNGS-FABRIK. An army-equipment factory, in the 1916 volume. Recorded, not interpreted.

column1: the Berlin hypothesis is weakened and the Szubin one is unchanged
column2: Szubin remains 190 death units across three offices with no alphabetical index, which is why the row costed it as bad value. NOTHING HERE MAKES IT CHEAPER. What has changed is that the alternative has been tested and is empty.

column1: the one Berlin route still untried, and it is not a directory
column2: the BERLIN DEATH INDEXES themselves, Standesamt Berlin I to XIII, for a man who could have died between 1884 and about 1930 as a non-householder. That is a very large read and it should not be started until something narrows it. A DEATH IN SCHUBIN BEFORE HIS SONS LEFT remains the simplest explanation of every negative held.

column1: what is image-read and what is not
column2: THE 1916 RUN IS READ AT THE IMAGE. 1903, 1905, 1908, 1910, 1913 and 1920 are text-layer readings, licensed by the 1916 agreement and by a Schmidt control in every volume, and are published as text-layer readings. The 1873-1896 observations are text-layer and are published only as counts and surnames, never as a forename negative.
